newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Four men killed by lightning in South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Four men killed by lightning in South Africa.

text.p: Four men were killed by lightning at a tribal leader's hut in South Africa's far north, prompting superstitious residents to vow retribution, police said on Wednesday.
The men, aged between 50 and 55, were drinking home-made beer in the thatched hut in the Doornfontein area of Northern Province on Tuesday afternoon when the lightning struck.
Three others were hurt, and were treated for minor injuries.

"The community was apparently angered by the incident and this prompted the police to deploy visible foot patrols in the area to prevent any unlawful acts which may arise," spokesman Captain Frans Mojapelo said in a statement.
The tribal leader, called an Induna, was not among the dead. Police did not say if he had been one of those injured.
Northern Province -- bordering on Mozambique and Zimbabwe -- is one of two of South Africa's nine provinces where ancient superstitions are prevalent.

Recent police statistics show 676 witchcraft-related cases -- which include incidents of arson, attempted murder, fingering people as witches and assault -- were recorded between January and June this year in Northern Province.
An old superstition is that when someone is struck by lightning, another person in the village has made that happen.
